# lazy-layers-cache

> A focused TypeScript hybrid L1/L2 cache for Node.js with lazy loading, stampede protection, fail-open resilience, size-tiered compression, and distributed invalidation over Redis Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ, or NATS.

LazyLayers is a caching library for Node.js. It starts as an in-process LRU cache with no infrastructure, and grows into a distributed cache layer as you need one: a shared Redis tier, an event bus that keeps every instance in agreement, and a binary wire format that cuts what you store.

Two methods do almost all the work:

- `getOrSet(key, loader)` — read through the layers, load once if nothing has it.
- `delete(key)` — invalidate everywhere. Every instance drops the key.

## Core Concepts

- L1 is an in-process LRU memory cache (via lru-cache). Holds live JavaScript objects. Nanosecond reads.
- L2 is a shared Redis store (via ioredis). Holds MessagePack bytes. Millisecond reads.
- The event bus carries invalidations between instances. Three event types: del, pattern, set.
- The `set` event broadcasts getOrSet loader results so peers populate L1 without a second loader call.

## Key Features

- Lazy loading with getOrSet(key, loader) — one loader call per key across all concurrent callers
- In-flight promise deduplication prevents same-process dogpile (stampede protection)
- Optional Redis-backed distributed lock for cross-instance stampede protection
- Fail-open resilience: L2 and event-bus failures are logged and swallowed, local L1 continues serving
- Stale fallback: last-known-good values returned on loader errors or timeouts
- Negative caching: loader misses briefly cached to avoid hammering databases
- Circuit breakers for L2 and event-bus publish, with configurable failure thresholds and cooldowns
- Soft and hard timeouts: soft returns stale immediately, hard aborts the loader
- Distributed invalidation over Redis Pub/Sub, RabbitMQ durable queues, NATS core, or NATS JetStream
- Size-tiered binary compression: none (< 256 B), lz4 (256 B–4 KB), zstd (4 KB+) with automatic codec selection
- 20+ typed cache events for metrics, logs, and tracing
- Live observability dashboard at /observelazyily (opt-in, zero-dependency)
- Built-in Prometheus /metrics endpoint with bounded cardinality
- OpenTelemetry/APM telemetry via node:diagnostics_channel
- TypeScript native with ESM and CommonJS builds
- Requires Node.js 20 or 22+

## Quick Start

```bash
npm install lazy-layers-cache
```

```ts
import { LazyLayersCache } from "lazy-layers-cache";

const cache = new LazyLayersCache<string, User>({
  ttlMs: 60_000,
  levels: {
    L1: { maxEntries: 1_000, ttlMs: 10_000 },
  },
  inflight: { enabled: true, ttlMs: 5_000 },
});

const user = await cache.getOrSet(`user:${id}`, async () => {
  return db.users.findById(id);
});
```

## Event Buses

| Transport | Delivery | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Redis Pub/Sub | At-most-once, ephemeral | Fastest option, zero extra infra, missed invalidations recover via TTL |
| RabbitMQ | Durable, retryable | Cannot afford to miss invalidations across reconnects |
| NATS Core | At-most-once, fastest | Low-latency fanout, no replay needed |
| NATS JetStream | Durable, replayable | Need durable delivery with ack, replay, and per-instance consumers |

## Serialization

Size-tiered binary compression with 4-byte magic prefixes for O(1) decode:

| Size | Codec | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| < 256 B | none | Compression makes small payloads bigger |
| 256 B – 4 KB | lz4 | Smaller and ~5x faster than zstd at these sizes |
| 4 KB+ | zstd | 767 B/µs savings at 256 KB; falls back to lz4 on Node 20 |
